title: CRISPR-Cas9 off-target prediction and budgeted evidence triage
authority_ceiling: Literature-derived research contract only; no biological, clinical, safety, or experimental authority

sources.note: The companion code reproduces analysis from standardized tool outputs; it does not rerun every tool in its native environment. Code license is not automatically a data license.

sources.relevance: Existing uncertainty-aware CRISPR off-target prediction and calibration method; include as a qualified specialist comparator where permitted and reproducible.
sources.novelty_boundary: This project does not claim novelty for uncertainty modelling. The proposed contribution is a deterministic evaluation contract for selective-risk, calibration, unknown-label bounds and context-stratified policy comparisons.
sources.note: Publication results have not been reproduced in this project; do not infer Symthaea improvement from the paper.

sources.relevance: Supports explicit treatment of interval-valued objectives and interval Pareto relations rather than reducing uncertainty to a point estimate.
sources.note: This literature does not validate the CRISPR implementation, its intervals, or any biological claim.

sources.relevance: Illustrates that uncertainty/coverage under covariate shift depends on assumptions and support overlap.
sources.note: This publication has not been reproduced by this project and is not validation evidence for Symthaea.

metric_planes.definition: Whether a native genome-wide search method nominates measured positive sites before any positive seeding
Ranking performance conditional on one exact, declared candidate universe; report whether validated positives were seeded
Analytical sensitivity/precision of an experimental nomination/confirmation method under its exact assay and study conditions
Candidate-site review burden required to achieve preregistered ranking/recall criteria
Worst/best-case assignment of unknown/unassayed candidate labels within one exact, declared candidate universe; not a confidence interval and not a bound on candidates omitted from that universe

symbols.U: unknown/unassayed candidates in the fixed candidate universe

limitations: requires P > 0 for recall bounds and K > 0 with at least K candidates for precision bounds
bounds apply only to unknown labels inside the fixed candidate universe
cannot bound true positives omitted by every candidate nomination method
not a probability, confidence interval, posterior estimate or safety guarantee

metric_planes.definition: Nondominated policies under a preregistered vector of task-relevant metrics, without universal score weights
metric_planes.acceptance: All compared policies use same preregistered objective definitions, units, direction, episodes, and availability rules. Missing metrics are not zero-filled. Pareto membership is not by itself a performance win or biological/clinical safety finding.

metric_planes.definition: Calibration quality and selective error-risk as a policy abstains on lower-confidence cases; report separately by declared biological/measurement context.
rules: Unknown/unassayed outcomes are excluded from proper-scoring-rule denominators, counted explicitly, and never converted into negatives.
Risk at each coverage reports observed-label risk and best/worst error bounds assigning unknown accepted labels correctly or incorrectly.
Exact confidence ties are accepted as a whole tier; probabilities and confidence thresholds are frozen before holdout reveal.
Calibration is not estimable within a context with no valid measured labels.
Calibration summaries are conditional on label ascertainment and are not clinical safety guarantees.

metric_planes.definition: Select unknown outcome labels to measure when their result can directly change the paired top-K positive-hit-count numerator for a frozen comparison of two policies.
rules: Input must be the same complete candidate universe ranked fully and uniquely under both policies, with the same fixed K.
Compute policy-exclusive membership from ranks and select UnknownUnassayed candidates only; do not accept caller-asserted disagreement flags.
Cheapest-first is optimal only for maximizing the count of equal-unit differential labels measured under the declared cost budget.
Report unknown candidates with same top-K membership separately; this planner does not resolve their denominator/absolute-recall uncertainty.
Compare with random, score/confidence-first, and top-ranked-unknown baselines at equal budget.
Cost units are proxies; do not infer laboratory savings or expected value of information.

metric_planes.definition: Conservative Pareto relation analysis on objective intervals to distinguish definite dominance from possible-only dominance and unresolved trade-offs.
rules: Intervals must be generated by a separately documented, preregistered procedure.
Robust dominance requires the candidate's worst bound to be no worse than the competitor's best bound in every objective and strictly better on at least one.
Possible-only dominance is not a performance win; preserve it in a separate output.
Coordinate-wise intervals do not encode covariance, pairing, or simultaneous coverage.
A larger robust frontier may correctly indicate insufficient evidence to distinguish policies.
Computational endpoint dominance cannot be interpreted as biological or clinical safety.

primary_impact_alternatives.target: At least +5 absolute percentage points in macro Recall@K vs best fair baseline on preregistered held-out guide/Cas9 groups
primary_impact_alternatives.caveat: Must report precision and false negatives; requires a group-aware uncertainty interval.

primary_impact_alternatives.target: At least 20% fewer candidate review slots to achieve the baseline's preregistered recall target
primary_impact_alternatives.caveat: Candidate slots are a review-burden proxy, not measured laboratory cost or treatment-price reduction.

aspirational_engineering_targets.inferential_rule: Describe improvement as demonstrated only if the preregistered interval excludes no improvement; otherwise report inconclusive/null.
aspirational_engineering_targets.external_generalization: Require at least one independent, use-permitted cohort before claiming robustness across datasets.
aspirational_engineering_targets.safety_rule: No model score, rank improvement, or cryptographic receipt implies a guide, editor, or therapy is safe.

measurement_allocation.target: At equal declared cost budget, resolve at least 20% more policy-differential unknown labels than random allocation on preregistered synthetic/stress-test episodes where estimable.
measurement_allocation.caveat: The metric resolves only the direct paired top-K numerator component; it is not full uncertainty reduction, expected value of information, experimental savings, or biological safety.

preconditions: identical candidate ID universe for both policies
same latent outcome assignment for each unknown candidate across policies
same eligible measured-positive reference and K

symbols.d: known-positive hits in A top K minus B top K
symbols.a: unknown IDs selected by A but not B
symbols.b: unknown IDs selected by B but not A
symbols.n: all remaining unknown IDs selected by both or neither

lower_bound.denominator: P + b + (n when d - b > 0, else 0)

upper_bound.denominator: P + a + (n when d + a < 0, else 0)

paired_label_sensitivity.claim_rule: A positive paired worst-case lower bound supports label-robust superiority only within the fixed candidate universe. If bounds span zero, describe any supported statistical gain as observed-label improvement, not label-robust improvement.
limitations: not a statistical confidence interval or posterior
cannot account for true sites omitted from every nomination method
does not establish biological safety or clinical utility

paired_label_sensitivity_formula_check.result: Closed-form bounds matched exhaustive label-assignment extrema in every tested case.
paired_label_sensitivity_formula_check.scope_limit: Formula design checked; Rust implementation and biological source benchmark remain unexecuted.

measurement_allocation_cost_optimality_c.result: Cheapest-first maximized the number of selected unit-value candidates under every enumerated budget; zero mismatches against exhaustive subset enumeration.
measurement_allocation_cost_optimality_c.scope_limit: This validates the narrow cheapest-first cardinality rule only. It does not compile or test the Rust source, verify rank input from a real source cohort, estimate expected value of information, or establish biological/clinical benefit.

interval_frontier_fixture.scope_limit: Independent interval arithmetic on F11 only; no Rust execution or statistical/biological validation.

interval_relation_exhaustive_oracle.result: Coordinate-wise possible and robust dominance formulas matched exhaustive endpoint evaluation for every tested interval pair.
interval_relation_exhaustive_oracle.scope_limit: This validates relation semantics for the enumerated two-objective intervals only. It does not compile or test the Rust module, derive statistical confidence intervals, handle covariance/joint coverage, or establish biological/clinical validity.
